name: Prose
purpose: Apply finished descendant typography, rhythm, and readable measure to trusted React content.
useWhen: An application, CMS adapter, or Markdown renderer already produced trusted React children that need coherent editorial typography.

avoidWhen.condition: Content is untrusted or still needs HTML or Markdown parsing.
avoidWhen.useInstead: an application-owned sanitizer and parser before Prose

avoidWhen.condition: A small explicit piece of interface copy needs one recipe.

composition: Pass trusted native React descendants to Prose and let the application own document structure, trust, and data loading.
Use direct Brick components when richer anatomy or behavior is needed; their classes intentionally override Prose's low-specificity descendant styles.

rules.statement: Sanitize and parse untrusted external content before it becomes Prose children; Prose never makes raw HTML safe.
Keep heading hierarchy, landmark choice, link destinations, table headers, language, and alternative text application-owned.
Use the narrow, default, wide, or none reading measure intentionally rather than adding duplicate width CSS.

Use direct Link, List, Blockquote, Code Block, Table, or Image components when their richer public contract is required, including accessible preserved horizontal scrolling for source or complex tables.
Load styles.css or core.css plus prose.css.

commonMistakes.mistake: Passing unsanitized HTML through dangerouslySetInnerHTML inside Prose.
commonMistakes.correction: Keep trust and sanitization in the application, then render trusted React children.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using Prose as a generic spacing wrapper around interface controls.
commonMistakes.correction: Use Stack and Text for interface composition; reserve Prose for editorial descendants.

validation: Confirm native descendant semantics and source order remain unchanged.

Confirm size and measure, headings, lists, links, quotes, tables, code, media, dark appearance, forced colors, narrow widths, zoom, text spacing, localization, RTL, SSR, refs, and modular CSS delivery.
